brief: Tonight is Pull B, and it is your sixth training day in a row. The recovery trainer's first choice was to give you today off. I overruled him and sent you in, because your rest between sets has not drifted, nothing in your notes hurts, and your numbers went up two nights running — chest press to 180 for eight last night is the best pressing you have logged. But I took his cut on the one lift he named. The bent-over row runs three sets instead of four: skip the 115 opener and start at 135, then 145, then 150 for nine, which is the top set you already own. Close-grip pulldown finally moves — you held 120 for ten on all three sets, the top of the range every time, so it goes to 127.5 for eight. Straight-arm pulldown, shrugs and incline curls stay exactly where they are; on all three the next weight up is a jump your log has not paid for yet, so chase one more rep per set instead and the weight comes when every set hits the top. Reverse curls come down one pin to 32.5. At 37.5 your reps fell to twelve, eleven, ten — the last two under what that slot even asks for — so three clean sets of twelve at the lighter pin is the honest version, and 37.5 comes back once you are finishing fifteens. Tomorrow is a rest day. One more thing: I asked yesterday and it did not happen, so I am asking once more and then leaving it alone — step on the scale before you start. Your only reading on file is 206 from 21 July, and you are seven months out.

flags.note: Tonight is your sixth training day in a row — the recovery trainer wanted you to rest today, and tomorrow is a rest day either way.
The Smith machine was taken on Sunday. If it is busy again tonight, run the bent-over row with a barbell at the same weights rather than losing the lift.
One bodyweight reading on file (206 lb, 21 July) and one cardio session in the last two weeks — both are the weakest part of your prep right now.

proposals.why: Push A now holds the only face pulls left in your week, the ones you wrote "Do you have a brain?" next to on 31 July, and this puts the reverse pec deck in that slot instead — it works the same back of the shoulder, and it is the machine you have carried from 82.5 to 90 without missing a set.

This is not the cut to two sets you turned down yesterday — Legs A asks for four calf sets and you have done two, two and three, and the weight only moves when you finish every set the plan asks for, so your 280s can never earn the next step; this makes the plan say three, which is what you actually do.

dissent.progression: Both opening sets finished at the top of the range last time, so raise them and run all four: 120, 140, 145, 150.
dissent.recovery: Heaviest spinal-loaded pull of the week, three days after deadlifting 265 for five with no rest day since — cut to three sets, drop the 115 opener, keep the top set.
dissent.why: I already overruled recovery on the bigger question by sending him in on day six at all, and this row is the exact lift he named as the reason. It is the only systemic load on tonight's card, so it is where the day's fatigue actually gets paid for, and his version keeps the top set intact so nothing that matters is lost. Adding five pounds to two ramp sets on the sixth straight day buys almost nothing against that.

dissent.progression: At 37.5 the reps fell to 12, 11, 10 — the last two under the slot's own 12-rep floor — so drop one pin to 32.5 and run three sets inside the range.
dissent.recovery: The only Pull B lift showing decay inside itself, and he did six biceps sets on 1 August — keep 37.5 and cut to two sets.
dissent.why: Both seats agree the lift is failing; they disagree on which knob. Recovery's cuts are aimed at systemic and spinal load, and one set of cable reverse curls at the end of the night costs nothing on that front — the row is where that argument gets paid. What is actually broken here is that 37.5 has never held the rep range, and keeping it for two sets leaves the load wrong and only hides the evidence. Dropping the pin fixes the real fault and lets the weight be earned back.

overrides.reason: Three sets tonight instead of four — this is the heaviest spinal-loaded pull of your week and it lands three days after deadlifting 265 for five, on your sixth training day in a row. The 115 opener comes off; your top set stays.
You held 120 for ten on all three sets last Pull B, the top of the range every time, so this takes the next machine step to 127.5 and asks for eight.
Last time was 13, 12, 12 at 37.5 — inside the range but not at the top of it, and the next pin on this machine is 45, a jump your log has not earned. Same weight, one more rep per set.
The 70s went 14, 13, 13 and the rack jumps straight to 80 with nothing in between. Stay on 70 and chase fifteen on all three sets; the 80s are yours when you get them.
Two sets cleared 25 for ten and the third stopped at nine. The next dumbbell is 30, too big a jump for one missing rep — close all three at ten tonight and the 30s come next time.

At 37.5 your reps fell away to 12, 11, 10 — the last two below the twelve this slot asks for. One pin down to 32.5 puts all three sets back inside the range, and the weight comes back once you are finishing fifteens there.
